title: KFin Technologies Ltd - 543720 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: KFin Q2 FY27: consolidated revenue up 30% QoQ including Ascent (10% ex-Ascent); EBITDA margin 40% incl. Ascent, 45.8% ex-Ascent; FY27 guidance held.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue up about 30% QoQ including Ascent and about 10% excluding it, with expenses up only 3% QoQ. Consolidated EBITDA margin was 40% including Ascent and 45.8% excluding it, and PAT crossed Rs. 100 crore (up 33% YoY, 7.5% QoQ per the call). Management said FY27 estimates are unchanged despite a recent market correction, citing buffers from discretionary spend deferrals. Ascent (Middle East exposure about 25% of its revenue) remained a drag on margins and client additions were flat.

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue from operations QoQ growth (incl. Ascent)

financial_highlights.change: up 33% YoY for the quarter; 7.5% YoY per management's wording; H1 PAT growth about 3% YoY

financial_highlights.metric: PAT margin incl. Ascent / excl. Ascent

segments.name: Mutual fund (domestic RTA)
segments.commentary: About 52% of revenue; AUM-linked. Management said yields rose about 2% QoQ on asset mix and AMC growth, and expects yields to stay broadly consistent. KFin AUM grew 15% vs industry 13%; market share above 33% overall and about 37% on SIPs.

segments.name: Issuer solutions
segments.commentary: About 13% of revenue; value-added services (7.5% of total revenue) spiked in Q2 on AGM/e-voting and corporate actions. Management guides about 20% YoY growth for the year, with Jio Platforms IPO handled as RTA.

segments.name: International (GFS, ex-Ascent)
segments.commentary: About 20% of revenue including Ascent. Management said 18 new client transitions are pending go-live in the next one to two quarters; international pipeline about US$47 million, up from about US$20 million 12 months earlier.

segments.name: Ascent (fund administration, Singapore/Middle East)
segments.commentary: Revenue growing 30%+ in each operating geography; EBITDA margin about 8% this quarter vs 7-7.5% last quarter and about minus 12% a year earlier. Management targets double-digit margin in the next couple of quarters and about 20% next fiscal year.

segments.name: Other businesses (alternatives, pensions, wealth)
segments.commentary: About 7% of revenue. Pensions grew 42% YoY vs industry 12-13% and broke even about three quarters ago; management said margins for these businesses are transitional due to ongoing transition costs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 18-20%, EBITDA margin 40-45% and PAT margin 25-30% (closing remarks); management said FY27 consolidated margin target is 40% on a full-year average, not exit rate.
Management said it does not need to change estimates for this quarter or next unless the market downturn is protracted.
Issuer solutions expected to grow about 20% YoY for the year, with upside to 20%+ if large IPOs such as Jio Platforms come through.
Expected GIFT City migration to give a 20-year tax holiday, timing not guided.
New Hyderabad office operational from 1 December: about Rs. 7 crore impact in FY27 and about Rs. 18 crore in FY28, with rent of about Rs. 80 lakh per month for 15 years.
capex_capacity: Aria.AI 2.0 and FinEx (mutual fund platform) rollouts; about 30-35% of mutual fund use cases deployed, with nearly all transformational platforms targeted by end of Q4 FY27.
Issuer solutions, pensions and wealth platforms to go live within about three months (by January).
International business replatforming (GFS) under way; Ascent to be re-platformed onto KFin's proprietary platform.
New Hyderabad office rent and operating lease start 1 December; cumulative lease period 9 years.
demand_pricing: Management said yields are expected to remain largely consistent, citing pricing discipline (about half of yield drivers), AMC mix (about 30%) and asset class mix.
Management said about 80% of funds managed are Category 3 funds exposed to public markets; passive share of KFin clients is above industry.
Ascent: about 80-90 contracted funds not yet launched; Q2 client additions flat due to fund managers holding launches amid Middle East conflict; net retention highest ever.
Management said large Ascent deals of around US$1 million deliver roughly 2x the margin of five US$200,000 deals with similar revenue.
Concentration: GFS top five clients about 23-24% of GFS revenue (largest about 5%); domestic top client about 5.5-6%, expected to fall to 2-2.5% in 18-24 months.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sequential MF yield stabilisation and will it hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yields rose about 2% QoQ on pricing discipline, AMC mix and asset mix; it expects yields to stay largely consistent based on visibility into late October.

qa_highlights.question: Can issuer solutions strength continue through the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided about 20% YoY issuer solutions growth, with corporate actions concentrated in Q2 and some spillover into Q3; IPO revenue is under 2% of issuer solutions revenue annually.

qa_highlights.question: What are the buffers if capital markets worsen?
qa_highlights.answer: Discretionary transformation, IT, automation, geographic expansion and product launch spend can be deferred if financials weaken, with some budgeted spend over the next five months at risk of deferral.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Ascent employee cost keep rising and when will its margin ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Ascent's EBITDA margin was about 8% vs 7-7.5% last quarter; it targets double digits in a few quarters and about 20% next fiscal year, with KFin-level margins in two more years. Standalone Ascent EBITDA is positive and cash breakeven gap is about Rs. 3.5-4 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the tax rate rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Loss-making new entities (KFin services, GIFT City, Thailand) have no deferred tax recognised, and Ascent's Singapore losses prevent foreign tax credit, so the rate is above 25.64% for KFin India; GIFT City migration timing is not guided.

qa_highlights.question: Why were Ascent client additions flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fund managers delayed launches amid market conditions; 80-90 contracted funds are awaiting launch in the coming weeks, and H2 is seasonally stronger for Ascent.

risks_watch: Market downturn: management said estimates hold unless the correction is protracted; capital-market-linked revenue and AUM mark-to-market are exposed.
Middle East conflict affecting about 25% of Ascent revenue and fund launch timing.
Philippines pension deal: neither awarded nor cancelled; management hopes to resolve within weeks.
Q3/Q4 corporate action revenue normally lower after Q2; issuer solutions growth depends on IPO pipeline including Jio Platforms.
Rising cloud, infra, memory and compute costs partly offsetting productivity gains in the MF business.
Deferred tax on loss-making entities keeps the effective tax rate above normal until GIFT City migration.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term trajectory and on Q2 execution, but cautious on near-term markets; management repeatedly said it is holding estimates while acknowledging headwinds from the recent correction and Middle East conflict. Evasive on exact product-level margins and yield-level detail, deferring to IR for splits.
key_quotes: And even as I look at our upcoming forecast for this quarter and the subsequent quarter, despite the headwinds, I am still confident that we do not have to change any of the estimates at this point in time, unless there is a continual protracted downturn from here on as well.
As per our base case, we will touch double digits, and we are looking at about 20% plus thereabouts into the next fiscal year.
So, no, it is average. It is not the run rate on Q4.
The growth in revenue will continue to be in the range of 18% to 20% with EBITDA margins in the range of 40% to 45%, and PAT margins in the range of 25% to 30%.

adds.what: New Hyderabad office (operational from 1 December; ~Rs. 80 lakh/month rent, 15-yr lease per brief; 9-yr cumulative lease per capex notes)
Issuer solutions, pensions and wealth platforms going live (by January)

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth held at 18-20% (midpoint 19%) with Issuer solutions guided ~20% and an 18-pending-client international pipeline (~US$47m) as support; backing is partial as no capacity additions are sized, and Q2 revenue ex-Ascent grew about 10% QoQ.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Ascent EBITDA margin rose to about 8% from 7-7.5% last quarter and targets double digits in a couple of quarters; consolidated margin was 40% vs about 34% in Q1 FY27, but management guides a 40% full-year average, not exit rate, so margin gains depend on Ascent ramp and the Hyderabad lease (about Rs. 7 crore FY27 impact) offsetting.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: New Hyderabad office goes live 1 Dec with about Rs. 80 lakh/month rent and 9-year cumulative lease, but no capacity utilisation or capacity sizing was disclosed, so this is a cost-led footprint add rather than volume capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided at 18-20% and Q2 revenue ex-Ascent grew about 10% QoQ; 18 international client transitions are pending go-live in 1-2 quarters and the international pipeline is about US$47m vs about US$20m a year earlier, though Ascent client additions were flat in Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed and no utilisation figure was given, so there is no basis for a new capex announcement call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 revenue growth at 18-20% and EBITDA margin at 40-45% despite a strong Q2 and explicitly said estimates are unchanged amid the market correction, so no upgrade signal.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management said estimates hold unless the market downturn is protracted; capital-market-linked revenue and about 25% Ascent Middle East exposure with flat Q2 Ascent client additions are the exposures, while Q3/Q4 corporate-action revenue normally falls after Q2.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Aria.AI 2.0 and FinEx rollouts with nearly all transformational platforms targeted by end Q4 FY27 (about 30-35% of MF use cases deployed now), plus issuer solutions, pensions and wealth platforms going live within about three months.

rows.label: Ascent 80-90 contracted funds awaiting launch
rows.why: 80-90 contracted funds not yet launched and H2 is seasonally stronger for Ascent, though Q2 client additions were flat as fund managers held launches amid the Middle East conflict.

rows.label: MF yield stability
rows.why: Yields rose about 2% QoQ on pricing discipline and AMC mix (about 30% of yield drivers) and management expects them broadly consistent, with about 80% of funds in Category 3 exposed to market moves.

rows.label: Philippines pension deal award
rows.why: Neither awarded nor cancelled; management hopes to resolve within weeks, so a win would add to the pensions/other businesses where margins are still transitional.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q2 execution, the medium-term trajectory and the 40% full-year margin target, but cautious on near-term markets, Middle East exposure and Ascent launch timing; analysts pushed on the tax rate, Ascent ramp and yield sustainability.
